### base metals: Greece is the word, but the pain could be in spain For most metals, we have noted a narrowing of trading ranges, particularly for those metals in over supply. The other feature is that price movements have generally reflected our view of the underlying fundamentals, with aluminium and nickel retreating significantly from the highs seen earlier this year. The decline in lead and zinc has been more gradual, despite the increase to reported stocks. however, the dominant force behind the metals and wider derivatives and financial markets continues to be developments in the eurozone debt crisis, with Greece taking centre stage, but post the Greek election investors are re-focusing on the spanish debt problem; the recent €100 billion package for spanish banks doesn’t appear to have allayed the market’s concerns. increased uncertainty as the Greek elections approached weighed on markets and investor disquiet continued to spill over, with spanish 10 year bond yields breaching and remaining above 7%, the level that triggered bailouts for Greece, ireland and Portugal. at the time of going to press, the worst case scenario appeared to have been avoided, with a pro-euro victory in Greece, albeit within a coalition structure. however, the efficacy of any austerity policy going forward remains questionable and the financial markets

still appear unconvinced on a wider level, with spain still in the firing line. We could thus be in a brief period of shortcovering and price recovery before both eurozone and wider global economic growth concerns return to the fore. inevitably, the base metals complex has continued to be at the mercy of macro sentiment, with particular focus on the travails dogging the eurozone, but also a less positive outlook for china. The recent 25 basis point cut in chinese interest rates (the first since 2008) provided only a brief fillip, as it preceded a raft of less than encouraging economic data from china. industrial production, manufacturing Pmi and fixed asset investment all undershot consensus, while retail sales continued to weaken. recent developments have seen prices move much closer towards our lower case projections. From a demand perspective, the two key issues are the recession pressures within the eurozone and the slower growth within china. in line with our expectations, the trade data highlight the slowdown in chinese consumption. This reflects both the weaker economic data and the build up in inventories; plus the variety of economic concerns, which have broadened since we last analysed our market balance and price projections. in terms of our price forecasts, we expect that prices will gravitate closer towards our low case projections; the two key underlying fundamental factors are demand conditions in china and europe, and also the slow response by producers to the changing market environment. in particular, the weakest markets from a supply perspective continue to be aluminium and nickel, but neither has seen any action on output that could significantly benefit their market balances. recent aluminium production cutbacks announced in henan have been followed by reports that the local government may discount electricity prices to producers, preventing any further curtailments. also, some other western smelters that have been under threat may be reprieved. ###### Base meTals & oTher commoDiTy Prices ###### Base meTal Prices iN maJor curreNcies 300

##### economic indicatoRs in march, the individual country oecD leading economic indicators mostly edged higher again, as they did during the first two months of the year. The overall oecD indicator rose to 100.5 from 100.4 in February. Whilst the united states, Japan and the Brics (bar russia) continue to post gains, the eurozone indicator has remained static since December 2011. We continue to assume that europe will remain a drag in the second quarter, with a negative impact on base metals demand. us consumer confidence, which had spiked to 71.6 in February, slid lower thereafter, posting 64.9 in may, the lowest level since December 2011. The deterioration in confidence was reflected in may us light vehicle sales; at an annualised rate of 13.778 million units, this was significantly down on the January-april average rate of 14.516 million. The us ism purchasing managers’ index, which had been rising since February, fell back in may to 53.5, from 54.8 in april. although inventories fell further, this was the only positive component of the index along with a continued rise in new orders. all other components were lower, including employment which had been on the increase. although we still expect an improvement in business confidence in the second half of the year, this will largely be dependent on further quantitative easing measures in both the developed and developing nations. eurozone industrial production fell 0.4% month-on-month in march after an against-trend rise of 0.7% in February. however, whilst German industrial production was 2.2% higher in march, month-on-month, it fell by 2.2% in april. similarly, italian industrial production, which rose 0.6% in march, slipped 1.9% in april. however, France reversed a 1.0% month-on-month fall in industrial production in march, posting a 1.5% increase in april. Further reinforcing the weak overall european economy, the eurozone Pmi declined to 45.1 in may, its lowest level since June 2009, indicating that most of the constituent country indices continue to show contraction. chinese industrial production grew 9.6% year-on-year in may, a slight improvement on april’s 9.3%, but lower than consensus expectation and well below the march figure of 11.9%. The chinese Pmi fell to 48.4 in may and fixed asset investment fell to 20.1% for the first five months, from 20.2% t

hrough april and 20.9% for the first quarter. although investment in mining sector remains robust, fixed asset investment is suffering from continued weakness in railway and transport and declining investment in real estate and power; all areas which are important for base metals demand. of further overall economic concern is the ongoing downward trend in chinese retail sales growth. Further reinforcing these figures was a 1.3% decline in auto sales for January-april and a one-year rmB26.5 billion stimulus measure to subsidise household electrical appliance purchases. Growth in the chinese consumer price index has also continued to fall for most of the year through may, to 3.0% year-on-year, from 4.6% in January. This does, however, provide the government with room to implement further interest rate cuts to follow the recent 25 basis point reduction, if necessary. indian industrial production jumped sharply to 6.6% growth month-on-month in march, from -1.3% and -1.7% in January and February, respectively. however, most reports suggest that the indian economy is in a slower phase as the capital goods, mining and manufacturing sectors remain especially weak. ###### oecD leaDiNG iNDicaTor & Base meTals iNDeX ###### chiNese iP GroWTh & Base meTals iNDeX 105 Thomson Reuters GFMS 400

###### market background markets have come under increased pressure as the potential for a Greek exit from the euro, and the disintegration of the currency have intensified, with spain next in the firing line. adding to the concerns has been slower growth in non-eurozone countries and, from a c

ommodity perspective, particularly china. the increasing likelihood of further monetary easing, if conditions worsen further, has prevented prices from going into freefall. the unexpected 25 basis point cut in china’s interest rate and the eu €100 billion package for spanish banks, had led to a bout of shortcovering with prices recovering from their lows. however, prices have since slipped further, as the impact of an announced cutback in production in henan was cushioned by a proposed electricity rate discount in the region. aluminium prices have fallen around 4% over the year to date, with the cash price trading around $1,900/tonne at the time of writing. at the same time, exchange stocks have recently been decreasing while physical premiums continue to post new record highs, to some extent cushioning producers from the falling price. ###### exchange stocks ease lower lme aluminium stocks have continued their recent downward trajectory, to 4.850 million tonnes. despite this, inventories held at the two main concentration points, detroit and vlissingen, have remained relatively steady since our last report, increasing their share of total stocks to a combined 50.6% (detroit 1.409 million tonnes; vlissingen – 1.045 million). total cancelled warrant inventories have also increased in recent days, with their share of the total reaching a new peak of 37.6% of the total, compared with 32% at the end of april. ###### weekly chanGe In lme stocks vs spot prIce 200000 2400
